alignments.note: Article before βρώσεως takes the English the (rule 19).
Substantival article supplies the nominal things and the genitive case preposition of rides with it (rules 21, 22); head on the nominal word.
εἰδωλοθύτων → sacrificed to idols, headed on the participial word.
Supplied subject rides with the verb; head on the lexical verb.

The clause is verbless with a noun subject and a negative predicate, so the supplied copula goes to the predicate (rules 53, 63). The ASV recasts the predicate οὐδέν as the discontinuous negation no … anything, both words realizing this one token under rule 15; marking the italicized anything added under rule 103 remains defensible, but nothing else licenses it and οὐδέν's own English is what it completes. This is why this clause is not analysed like the verse's second one: here the negative is the predicate, whereas οὐδείς below is attributive to its noun.

ἐν → in; the prepositional phrase is an adjunct here rather than the predicate, the ASV's own complement of the copula being anything, so rule 53's preposition carrier does not apply and the copula stays with οὐδέν.
Anarthrous κόσμῳ with a supplied determiner: no article competes, so the is an ordinary helper on the noun (rule 51).

Verbless existential clause expressing no subject of its own: the supplied subject there and the copula is ride with the predicate noun (rule 68), discontinuously across the attributive quantifier under rule 15. This is the same analysis this chapter gives εἷς θεός → there is one God at 1CO.8.6, and the same the corpus gives the identical frame at 1TI.2.5 (θεός → there is god, headed on the noun). Placing there is on οὐδείς remains defensible, but a quantifier standing inside the predicate phrase is a modifier and not the carrier, as rule 96 already holds for an article.

οὐδείς is attributive to θεός and keeps only its own English word no, exactly as εἷς keeps a bare one at 1CO.8.6. Rules 41, 59 and 87 decide where the English negation goes and say nothing about a supplied verb, so carrying the clause's negation does not make this token the carrier of the existential.
εἰ μή rendered by the single but: the conjunction answers to neither particle separately (rule 39), headed on the first particle and on the English word.

review_notes: The verse's two verbless clauses are analysed apart because the Greek differs, not because of the English. In οὐδὲν εἴδωλον ἐν κόσμῳ the negative is the clause's own predicate and rule 63 gives it the copula; in οὐδεὶς θεός the negative is attributive and θεός is the only nominal left, so the supplied existential rides with the noun under rule 68. The earlier reading, which placed there is on οὐδείς for parallelism with the first clause, split this chapter against 1CO.8.6's εἷς θεός → there is one God and against 1TI.2.5.

The italicized anything is folded onto οὐδέν rather than marked added: rule 103's test is licensing, and οὐδέν's own English is what the word completes. Marking it added remains defensible and is named here so a later reader can act on it.
v005 is a selected unit on r00-base covering s016 and takes no new textual decision here (rule 12).
